lessons.title: Your Radial Menu
lessons.summary: Open your tools right where you are drawing.

steps.title: Open the Radial Menu
steps.text: Tap the touch puck to open the radial menu. With Apple Pencil Pro, you can squeeze instead.

steps.title: Everything Within Reach
steps.text: The ring and the arcs fit the tool in hand: Smoothing and Clean Joins for the brushes, Gap for Fill, Turn and Flip for Stamp. Drag an arc to change it, or tap a tool in the centre. Tap the page when you are finished.

steps.title: Make It Yours
steps.text: Preferences > Radial Menu lets you choose what it shows, how large it is and which tools stay on it.
steps.opened: Radial Menu in this list sets what it shows, how large it is and which tools stay on it. Finish closes Preferences.

lessons.title: Same Gestures Everywhere
lessons.summary: Undo, redo, zoom and fit work the same on every canvas.

steps.title: Draw Something
steps.text: Draw a line or two on the practice page.

steps.title: Two Fingers Undo, Three Redo
steps.text: Tap the page with two fingers to undo, and with three to redo. Hold two fingers down to keep undoing until you lift them.

steps.title: Pinch, Twist and Slide
steps.text: Pinch to zoom in on the spot under your fingers, twist to turn the page, and drag with two fingers to move it.

steps.title: Fit and Go Back
steps.text: Double-tap with one finger to see the whole page. Pinch outward straight after and you are back where you were. A quick pinch inward fits too.

steps.title: The Same on Every Canvas
steps.text: Lattice, the 3D body, Print Stencil's preview, feedback screenshots and On a Photo use the same gestures, wherever they make sense.

lessons.title: Choose a Background
lessons.summary: Keep the page plain or add a living background.

steps.title: Plain by Default
steps.text: New installs start plain, so the app stays quick on every iPad. Open Preferences, then Background, to choose a living background.
steps.opened: Choose Background in this list to pick a living background. Finish closes Preferences.

lessons.title: Widget Tour
lessons.summary: See each Home Screen widget and how to add it.

steps.title: Add a Widget
steps.text: On your Home Screen, hold an empty spot until the icons wiggle. Tap Edit in the top corner, then Add Widget.

steps.title: Choose Bismuth Studio
steps.text: Pick Bismuth Studio in the list. Swipe across to see each widget and size, then tap Add Widget.

steps.title: Recent Drawings
steps.text: Shows the drawings you worked on last. Tap one to open it straight away. The larger sizes show up to six.

steps.title: Quick Start
steps.text: One tap starts a new drawing. The wider size also continues your last drawing, opens the gallery or opens Learn Bismuth.

steps.title: Daily Pattern
steps.text: A new symmetry idea each day. Tap it to start a new drawing with that symmetry already set up.

steps.title: Last Drawing
steps.text: Keeps the drawing you worked on last in view, with when you last edited it. Tap it to carry on.

steps.title: Private on the Lock Screen
steps.text: Drawing names and pictures on Recent Drawings are hidden while your iPad is locked.

lessons.title: Draw in Symmetry
lessons.summary: Turn one line into a balanced pattern.

steps.title: Open Pattern
steps.text: Tap the Pattern button in the top bar. Its picture and words show what is on.
steps.opened: The Pattern panel sits beside the page. Pictures from the gallery come first, then a section for each kind of pattern.

steps.title: Choose Your Segments
steps.text: Symmetry is the first section. Rotate repeats each line around the centre, and Segments sets how many copies you get.

steps.title: Add a Mirror
steps.text: Mirror reflects every line as well, for a perfectly balanced pattern.

steps.title: Try It
steps.text: Draw one line on the page and watch every copy appear. The panel can stay open while you draw.

lessons.title: Clean Joins
lessons.summary: Tidy the small overshoot where lines meet.

steps.title: Draw a Line
steps.text: Clean Joins is on for this lesson. Draw one line on the page.

steps.title: Cross It
steps.text: Draw another line that runs just past the first. The small overshoot is trimmed for you.

steps.title: Find the Switch
steps.text: Open the radial menu from the touch puck whenever you want to switch Clean Joins on or off.

lessons.title: Trim Loose Ends
lessons.summary: Cut a line back to the nearest crossing.

steps.title: Make a Crossing
steps.text: Draw two lines that cross, leaving a loose end past the crossing.

steps.title: Pick Trim
steps.text: Trim has its own button on the left toolbar, under the line tools. It is selected for you now.

steps.title: Cut It Back
steps.text: Scribble across the loose end. It cuts back to the nearest crossing.

lessons.title: Circle to Trim
lessons.summary: Remove a leftover dot or piece by circling it.

steps.title: Leave a Stray Mark
steps.text: Draw a short line or a dot away from the rest of your drawing.

steps.title: Circle It
steps.text: With Trim, draw a loop all the way around the stray mark. Everything wholly inside the loop is removed.

steps.title: Undo If Needed
steps.text: One undo brings back everything the loop removed.

lessons.title: Join Two Line Ends
lessons.summary: Circle two ends that nearly meet and they join in a clean point.

steps.title: Pick Join
steps.text: Tap Join on the left toolbar, just under Trim. It is the Trim tool in Join mode, so your mark shows in pink.

steps.title: Circle the Ends
steps.text: Circle, or scribble over, the spot where two line ends nearly meet. Both lines are carried on to one clean point. Ends that overshoot each other are cut back to the point instead.

steps.title: In a Pattern Too
steps.text: In a symmetry or wallpaper, circle the ends on any copy and every copy joins. If the ends are on another visible layer, Join finds them there and says which layer. Ends that already meet get a short message instead.

steps.title: Back to Cutting
steps.text: Tap Trim, just above, to cut again. One Undo takes a join back. You can also put Join on a radial menu dot, or find it in Loupe.

lessons.title: Mirror a Curve
lessons.summary: Draw one side of a petal and add the other.

steps.title: Draw One Side
steps.text: Draw a curve from the base of a petal to its tip and hold still at the end until it snaps smooth.

steps.title: Tap Mirror Curve
steps.text: A new button appears beside the puck. Tap it and the matching side is added, meeting at both ends.

steps.title: Any Line, Any Time
steps.text: Lasso a curved line and tap Mirror in the bar to do the same later. Tap Deselect, then one Undo takes it back.

lessons.title: Even Parallel Lines
lessons.summary: Add a line at a set distance from another.

steps.title: Draw an Outline
steps.text: Draw a closed shape or a single line on the page.

steps.title: Select It
steps.text: Lasso the line, or a whole outline, then tap Offset in the bar that appears. With several lines selected, each one gets its own offset.

steps.title: Set the Distance
steps.text: Drag Distance, or tap minus and plus for fine steps. Choose Outside or Inside. The preview line shows the result.

steps.title: Tap Done
steps.text: The new line is added in the same colour and width, with an even gap all the way round.

lessons.title: Dashes and Dots
lessons.summary: Turn any line into even dashes or dots.

steps.title: Draw a Line
steps.text: Draw a line or an outline on the page.

steps.title: Select It
steps.text: Lasso the line, then tap Dashes in the bar that appears.

steps.title: Set the Pattern
steps.text: Choose Dashes or Dots, then drag Length and Gap. The preview shows the result, and the number tells you how many pieces you will get.

steps.title: Tap Done
steps.text: The pattern is fitted to the line, so it starts and ends on a whole dash and a closed outline meets itself evenly. One Undo brings the line back.

lessons.title: Repeat a Copy
lessons.summary: Build an even row or ring from one copy.

steps.title: Select and Duplicate
steps.text: Lasso a shape, then tap Duplicate in the bar that appears.

steps.title: Place the First Copy
steps.text: Move, turn or resize the copy to where the next one belongs, then tap Done.

steps.title: Tap Repeat
steps.text: Each tap adds another copy by the same step, so the spacing stays even. Turn the copy for a ring, or turn and shrink it for a spiral.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Tap Done, or just keep drawing. Each copy is one Undo.

lessons.title: Repeat a Motif Along a Line
lessons.summary: Draw a line and a set number of motifs land evenly along it.

steps.title: Switch It On
steps.text: This one is experimental: switch on Motif Along a Line in Preferences, Experimental. Then pick the Stamp tool, tap it again to open your motifs, and switch on Along a Line.

steps.title: Choose How Many
steps.text: Set Count to the exact number of copies you want, such as seven. Size sets how big each one is. You can also drag the Count chip on the left toolbar.

steps.title: Draw the Line
steps.text: Draw a line anywhere on the page. A light preview shows where each copy will land. Lift, and the copies are placed evenly, with the first and last at the ends of your line.

steps.title: Loops and Direction
steps.text: End your line where it began and the copies spread evenly all the way round. Follow the Line turns each copy to match the line; switch it off to keep them upright. One Undo removes the whole set.

lessons.title: Colour a Lattice
lessons.summary: Pick colours for lines and points, and blend them level by level.

steps.title: Open Colour
steps.text: Open Lattice (the diamond beside the Pattern button). Tap the Lines or Points dot under Formations to choose that colour; the Colour section in the panel has the same, and the swatches in the top bar open it too.

steps.title: Pick a Colour
steps.text: Tap Lines or Points and pick a colour. The preview changes straight away. Use Pen Colour goes back to your pen's colour.

steps.title: Colour by Level
steps.text: Switch on Colour by Level (its own section, under Colour) and shape the gradient: the first level takes its left end and the deepest its right. Tap the strip to add more colours.

steps.title: Send It
steps.text: Tap Done at the top right to add it to this drawing as one layer group, or New Drawing to start a fresh page with it. Save to Lattices keeps it in the gallery; Export sends it as SVG, PDF or PSD.

lessons.title: Stack Formations in a Lattice
lessons.summary: Layer several shapes in one lattice, each with its own colour.

steps.title: Add a Formation
steps.text: Open Lattice. Beside Formations, tap the plus. A copy of your shape is added, turned half a step so you can see it.

steps.title: Shape Each One
steps.text: Tap a number to choose a formation. The sections below (Shape, Edges, Lines, Colour and the rest) now change only that one. Try a different number of points or a smaller radius.

steps.title: Give It a Colour
steps.text: Open Colour and pick a line colour. Each formation keeps its own colours.

steps.title: Explore
steps.text: Tap the dice for a random shape to start from, or the palette for random colours. The bin removes the chosen formation.

steps.title: Send It
steps.text: Done puts the lattice on the page as one layer group, with each formation on its own layers inside it, so you can still move and edit them apart.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Tap Done to add it to the drawing, or Canvas at the top left to leave without adding (it stays in Lattices). If you opened a saved lattice and changed it, choose Overwrite or Save as a New Lattice first.

lessons.title: Close My Line
lessons.summary: Finish near your start and the line joins up.

steps.title: Draw a Loop
steps.text: Draw a loop and finish near where you began. The line joins up for you.

steps.title: Curves Stay Curved
steps.text: Curves stay curved and straight sides stay straight where the ends meet.

steps.title: Change It
steps.text: Hold Clean Joins or Close My Line on the radial menu to switch Close My Line off, or to change how near you need to finish.

lessons.title: Steady Your Lines
lessons.summary: Use Smoothing and the rope to calm a shaky hand.

steps.title: Open the Radial Menu
steps.text: Tap the touch puck. Smoothing and the Rope Stabiliser are the small switches at either end of the ring, under their sliders.

steps.title: Hold for Settings
steps.text: Tap a switch to turn it on or off. Hold it to open the settings for that one control. Tap the page when you are finished.

steps.title: Try It
steps.text: Draw a slow, wavy line and see how it settles.

lessons.title: Fill a Shape with Small Gaps
lessons.summary: Fill closes tiny openings in a line for you.

steps.title: Draw a Shape
steps.text: Draw a closed shape on the page. A tiny gap where the ends meet is fine.

steps.title: Fill It
steps.text: Tap inside the shape. If a small gap would let the colour escape, Fill closes it and tells you.

steps.title: Larger Gaps
steps.text: For a wider opening, drag the Gap control on the left toolbar upward, then tap again.

lessons.title: Fill Through Outlines
lessons.summary: Fill a shape and its outline as one solid shape, or simplify a whole layer.

steps.title: Draw a Shape
steps.text: Draw a closed shape on the page.

steps.title: Fill Through
steps.text: Tap LINES on the left toolbar so it says Fill. Fill and Gradient Fill now take in the outline around the shape.

steps.title: Fill It
steps.text: Tap inside the shape. The outline becomes part of the fill, so one solid shape is left.

steps.title: A Whole Layer at Once
steps.text: Hold a layer in Layers and open Shapes and Lines. Simplify merges every fill with its outline; Convert to Shapes and Convert to Lines switch the whole layer between filled shapes and lines.

lessons.title: Fill Lots of Small Gaps
lessons.summary: Sweep or circle with Fill to fill many tiny gaps at once.

steps.title: Draw Some Gaps
steps.text: Draw a few lines close together, so there are small gaps between them.

steps.title: Tap Near a Gap
steps.text: With Fill, tap a thin gap. If your tap lands on a line, the nearest gap fills, at any zoom.

steps.title: Sweep Across Them
steps.text: Drag across several gaps. Every gap you touch fills, and one Undo takes them all back.

steps.title: Circle a Patch
steps.text: Draw a loop around a busy patch and finish where you started. Every closed gap inside the loop fills.

lessons.title: Drag Colour to Fill
lessons.summary: Fill a shape by dragging the colour onto it.

steps.title: Draw a Shape
steps.text: Draw a closed shape on the page.

steps.title: Drag the Colour
steps.text: Drag the colour circle at the foot of the left toolbar onto the shape, then let go. The shape fills and the Fill tool is now on.

steps.title: Keep Filling
steps.text: Tap more shapes to fill them with the same colour.

lessons.title: Export With Layers
lessons.summary: Open your drawing in Photoshop, Illustrator or Affinity with its layers.

steps.title: Open Export
steps.text: Tap Export at the top right. PNG and JPEG give you a picture; the three below keep your layers.
steps.opened: Choose SVG or PDF for a vector file, or Photoshop PSD for pixel layers. Your layer names come with them.

steps.title: Vector Files
steps.text: SVG and PDF keep every line as a path, sharp at any size. Use PDF for Illustrator or Affinity Designer, SVG for Inkscape, Figma or the web. Each layer comes in separately, with the paper on a layer you can hide.

steps.title: Photoshop Files
steps.text: PSD gives one pixel layer per Bismuth layer, with its name and opacity, plus a Paper layer you can hide. It takes a few seconds to prepare.

lessons.title: The Pattern Panel
lessons.summary: Every pattern in one panel beside the page.

steps.title: One Pattern Button
steps.text: The top bar has one Pattern button now. It lights up when a pattern is on and says which, like Kaleidoscope 8 · Hex Grid.

steps.title: Gallery First
steps.text: Pictures come first: tap one to use it, draw a test line, undo and try the next. See All opens the whole gallery.

steps.title: A Section for Each
steps.text: Symmetry, Wallpaper, Repeat, Grid, Fade and Constructions each have a switch and a one-line summary. Switching one on opens its controls; tap a name to open or fold it.

steps.title: One Switch for Every Pattern
steps.text: The switch beside the panel's title turns every pattern off at once, and on again exactly as it was, grid and all. The eye at the end of the Pattern button in the top bar does the same.

steps.title: Edit on Page
steps.text: Edit on Page, at the bottom, unlocks the guides so you can move and turn them. The panel stays beside the page while you do.

steps.title: Put It Where Your Hand Is Not
steps.text: Drag the small tab on the panel's top edge and targets appear: the left or right edge, or a corner. Drop it on one to dock it there, anywhere else to float. Tap the tab to fold it to a small bar. The pin keeps it open while you draw.

lessons.title: Dock Your Panels
lessons.summary: Put Pattern and Layers where your hand is not.

steps.title: Drag the Tab
steps.text: Open Pattern and drag the small tab on its top edge. Six targets appear: each edge and each corner, with an outline of where the panel will land.

steps.title: Drop to Dock
steps.text: Let go on a target to dock the panel there. Docked down an edge, the page slides aside so its centre stays in view. Let go anywhere else and the panel floats.

steps.title: Layers Too
steps.text: Layers has the same tab, fold and pin. Put it in a corner on the same side as Pattern, or on the other side.

steps.title: Your Drawing Hand
steps.text: Preferences, Pencil & Touch, Drawing Hand: choose Right-Handed or Left-Handed and every panel moves to the side away from your hand.

lessons.title: Edit a Pattern on the Page
lessons.summary: Move, turn and recentre your guides with the controls beside you.

steps.title: Open Pattern
steps.text: Tap the Pattern button in the top bar to open the Pattern panel beside the page.

steps.title: Edit on Page
steps.text: Tap Edit on Page at the bottom of the panel. Drawing pauses so you can set up your guides without making a mark.
steps.opened: The panel stays beside the page, so you can change Symmetry, Repeat or the grid and watch the guides as they change.

steps.title: Move, Turn and Recentre
steps.text: Drag the centre ring to move the guides and the small dot to turn them. Tap Recentre, or double-tap the ring, to put them back in the middle of the page.

steps.title: Start From a Picture
steps.text: The pictures at the top of the panel set everything at once; See All shows the whole gallery. When Rotate does not fit the grid, Make It Fit lines them up. Tap Done to draw.

lessons.title: Undo After Reopening
lessons.summary: Your last 50 steps stay with each drawing.

steps.title: Draw Something
steps.text: Draw a line or two on the practice page.

steps.title: Undo Later, Too
steps.text: Bismuth saves your latest steps with each drawing (50 to start with). Close it, open it again tomorrow, and Undo and Redo still go back through what you did.

steps.title: Choose How Many
steps.text: Open Preferences, then Drawing. Undo Steps under History sets how many steps each drawing keeps, up to 200, or Off.
steps.opened: Choose Drawing in this list, then scroll to History. Done closes Preferences.

lessons.title: Paint With Gradients
lessons.summary: Lay a gradient across the page, or colour a layer's lines with one.

steps.title: Gradient Fill
steps.text: Tap the Fill button twice and pick Gradient Fill. Drag across the page: the gradient runs from where you start to where you lift.

steps.title: Choose the Colours
steps.text: Tap GRADIENT on the left toolbar. Drag a handle to move a colour, tap the strip to add one, switch Radial, or pick a ready gradient. Start your drag on a filled shape to give just that shape the gradient.

steps.title: Gradient Lines
steps.text: Hold a layer in Layers and choose Line Colour: Gradient. Every line on that layer takes the gradient across the page; Page Reversed turns the page's own gradient round for a striking contrast.

steps.title: One Gradient Everywhere
steps.text: The Gradient Liner (Across the Page), Lattice's Colour by Level and the page background all use this same gradient control.

lessons.title: Clip a Pattern to a Shape
lessons.summary: Keep a pattern inside the shape below it.

steps.title: Draw the Shape
steps.text: Draw a closed shape for your pattern to stay inside.

steps.title: Fill It
steps.text: Tap inside the shape to fill it. A clipped layer only shows where this layer has ink.

steps.title: Add a Layer
steps.text: Add a new layer for the pattern.

steps.title: Switch On Clip
steps.text: Tap Clip so this layer only shows where the layer below has ink.

steps.title: Draw the Pattern
steps.text: Draw across the shape in the new colour. Anything outside it stays hidden.

steps.title: Print What You See
steps.text: Open Print Stencil. It follows your clipped layers, so the stencil matches the page.
steps.opened: The preview shows only what the clip keeps. Dotted lines are one of the line styles you can print. Finish closes this panel.

lessons.title: Cut Out with a Mask
lessons.summary: Show or hide part of the layer below.

steps.title: Draw the Pattern
steps.text: Draw the pattern you want to cut.

steps.title: Add a Layer
steps.text: Add a new layer for the mask.

steps.title: Choose the Mask
steps.text: Tap Mask to show the pattern inside your mask. Tap again to hide it there instead.

steps.title: Draw the Mask
steps.text: Draw over the pattern. Only the parts under your mask stay visible, and the mask itself never prints.

lessons.title: Print a Stencil
lessons.summary: Size a design for skin and print it.

steps.title: Open Print Stencil
steps.text: When your design is ready, Print Stencil prepares it for skin.
steps.opened: Tap Next for the settings that matter most.

steps.title: Set It Up
steps.text: Set the width on skin, switch on Mirror for Transfer if you need it, and check the preview before printing.

lessons.title: Line Up Your Stencil
lessons.summary: Add alignment marks and check for gaps that are too tight.

steps.title: Open Print Stencil
steps.text: Open Print Stencil, then scroll down to Marks and Checks.
steps.opened: Scroll down in this panel and open Marks and Checks.

steps.title: Alignment Marks
steps.text: Switch on Alignment Marks to print a centre cross and edge marks. They help you line the stencil up on the body, or with another sheet.

steps.title: Gap Check
steps.text: Smallest Gap sets how close lines may sit. A warning under the preview tells you when gaps may close up as the tattoo heals. The count is an estimate.

lessons.title: Send Feedback as You Test
lessons.summary: Mark up the screen and dictate notes.

steps.title: Start Feedback Mode
steps.text: Tap the speech bubble on the right-hand toolbar. A small bar stays on screen while you test, and glows until you tap Stop.

steps.title: Add a Note
steps.text: Tap Add Note and mark up the screenshot with the pen, highlighter, arrow, box or ring. Pick a colour and width from the bar, or tap the floating puck. Your artwork is hidden unless you choose to include it.

steps.title: Change a Colour
steps.text: Tap any mark you made, without dragging, and pick a new colour: it changes on the spot. Saved notes open again with their marks, so you can still change them.

steps.title: Type Right on the Screenshot
steps.text: Choose Text Note, tap where the problem is and type. Each note gets a number you can mention in your words. Drag a note to move it, and use Cover to hide anything private.

steps.title: Zoom In to Mark Small Things
steps.text: Pinch the screenshot to zoom, turn or slide it, then mark it up as usual. Tap Fit to see it all; pinch outward to go back. Two fingers undo, three redo.

steps.title: Send When Ready
steps.text: Review your notes and send them together. Claude reads them only if you switch that on.

lessons.title: Fill the Page and Change the Paper
lessons.summary: Fill an empty layer, colour the page, or give it a gradient, a paper texture or a picture.

steps.title: Fill an Empty Layer
steps.text: With Fill, tap the empty page. On an empty layer the open page fills at once, with no second tap.

steps.title: Colour the Page Itself
steps.text: Tap Fill on the left toolbar until it says Page. Now a tap colours the page under every layer, not a shape.

steps.title: Paper, Gradient or Picture
steps.text: In Layers, the Page row at the foot of the list holds the page background. Tap it.
steps.opened: Choose Paper, Colour, Gradient, Texture or Picture. Textures have Size, Grit and Strength; a gradient has handles to drag, tap or add. Exports keep the page as a Paper layer.

lessons.title: Type Right on the Page
lessons.summary: Type where you tap, type along a line, and turn text into shapes.

steps.title: Pick the Text Tool
steps.text: This one is experimental: switch on Text Tool in Preferences, Experimental. Then pick Aa on the left toolbar.

steps.title: Tap and Type
steps.text: Tap the page where the text should start and type. The letters appear right there, and Return starts a new line. Started with the Pencil, the keyboard stays down: write into the Text bar's field with Scribble.

steps.title: Face, Size and Spacing
steps.text: The Text bar sets size and alignment; picking a colour recolours the text. The radial menu has size and letter spacing on its arcs, and face, alignment and style on its ring.

steps.title: Change It Later
steps.text: With the Text tool, tap any text to change it, even after moving or turning it. The caret goes where you tap, and dragging selects letters.

steps.title: Type Along a Line
steps.text: Tap a line or a circle with the Text tool and the text follows it. On a circle it starts where you tapped. The arrows on the Text bar put it on the other side.

steps.title: Lift It Off the Line
steps.text: On a line, the Baseline button sets the text on, above or below the line, so a thick line never covers the letters. Drag the bracket at the start of the text to slide it along the line.

steps.title: Create Outlines
steps.text: Create Outlines turns text into plain shapes: filled text becomes one shape, Outline text a line round each letter. It also works on text you select with the lasso.

lessons.title: Pick a Colour from the Page
lessons.summary: Take any colour you can see, with a magnifier to aim.

steps.title: Pick the Eyedropper
steps.text: Pick the eyedropper on the left toolbar. The button in the colour panel does the same.

steps.title: Look Before You Touch
steps.text: Hover Apple Pencil over the page: a small magnifier follows the tip. The top of its ring is the colour under the centre, the bottom is the colour you have now.

steps.title: Drag to Aim, Lift to Pick
steps.text: Touch the page and drag. With a finger the magnifier sits above your finger so you can see. Lift to take the colour: it flies into the colour circle on the left.

steps.title: Anything on the Page
steps.text: It takes what you see: lines, fills, the paper and its texture, gradients, pictures and airbrush. Lift off the page and it tells you nothing was picked, and stays ready.

steps.title: Hold, Then Drag
steps.text: Without the toolbar: hold a finger on the page. Lift and the radial menu opens as always. Keep holding and drag instead, and it turns into the eyedropper; lift to pick.

lessons.title: See What a Setting Does
lessons.summary: Every line setting shows what it does, and you can try it before you draw.

steps.title: A Picture for Each Setting
steps.text: Hold Clean Joins on the radial menu. The picture at the top of the panel shows what the setting you touched last does, and redraws as you move its slider or switch it.

steps.title: Faint and Solid
steps.text: In each picture the faint line is what your hand drew, and the solid line is what Bismuth keeps.

steps.title: Try It
steps.text: Preferences, Drawing has a Try It pad. Draw across its dashed mirror line, then change any setting: your lines are finished again with it. Nothing you draw there touches your drawing.

steps.title: Same Everywhere
steps.text: Each setting has one name, icon and colour on the radial menu, in the stroke panel and in Preferences.

lessons.title: Loupe: Every Command in One List
lessons.summary: Find any action in a tap, sorted for the tool and layer in hand.

steps.title: Open Loupe
steps.text: This one is experimental: switch on Loupe in Preferences, Experimental. Then tap the magnifying glass at the top of the right toolbar.
steps.opened: This is Loupe. It opens on what fits what you are doing, so you rarely need to type.

steps.title: What You Are Doing Comes First
steps.text: Recent commands sit at the top, then your tool's switches (Smoothing, Clean Joins, the Eraser's Part or Whole), your layer's actions, and the Pattern panel's switches when a pattern is on. Tap any row to run it and Loupe closes.

steps.title: Choices Open a Second List
steps.text: Rows with an arrow, like Change Tool, Segments and Use a Pattern, open a list to pick from. The arrow at the top goes back.

steps.title: Search Without the Keyboard
steps.text: Write a word in the search box with Apple Pencil: Scribble turns it into text and the list narrows as you write. Words like mirror, layer, size or undo all work.

steps.title: Other Ways In
steps.text: Put Loupe on a dot around the radial menu with Edit Dots. With a keyboard, Command-K opens it ready to type. The up and down arrows move through the list, Return runs the highlighted row (or the top match), and Escape closes it.

lessons.title: Save Your Own Patterns
lessons.summary: Keep a pattern you like, with a name, for any drawing.

steps.title: Make a Pattern You Like
steps.text: Open Pattern and set it up: Symmetry, Repeat, Wallpaper, Grid, Fade. Switching a section on opens its controls.

steps.title: Tap the Bookmark
steps.text: The bookmark beside All Off saves it as My Pattern 1, first among the cards. No typing needed.

steps.title: Give It a Name
steps.text: Hold its card and choose Rename. Write the name with Apple Pencil or type it. Remove from My Patterns is there too.

steps.title: Use It Anywhere
steps.text: Your patterns stay first in See All under My Patterns, in every drawing, and in Loupe's Use a Pattern list.

lessons.title: Snap, Then Adjust
lessons.summary: Hold to snap a line or shape, then steer it before you lift.

steps.title: Snap a Line
steps.text: Draw a line and hold still at the end until it snaps straight. Keep the Pencil down.

steps.title: Steer the End
steps.text: Still holding, move the Pencil: the end follows. It catches every 15 degrees with a soft click. The Snap 15° switch beside the Pattern panel's angle sliders turns this off as well.

steps.title: Arcs Keep Their Circle
steps.text: Draw an arc and hold. Move round the circle to make it longer or shorter, or in and out to change its size. Lift to keep it.

steps.title: Shapes Turn and Grow
steps.text: Draw a circle or a square and hold. Move the Pencil to turn it and make it bigger or smaller.

steps.title: Ovals Into Circles
steps.text: Draw an oval and hold until it snaps. Still holding, touch the screen with a finger: the oval becomes a perfect circle. Lift the finger and it is an oval again. Lift the Pencil to keep the one you see.

lessons.title: Size the Gallery
lessons.summary: Pinch to see more drawings at once, or bigger.

steps.title: Pinch the Gallery
steps.text: In the gallery, pinch inward with two fingers for more, smaller cards, or outward for fewer, larger ones. Stacks and lattices change size with them.

steps.title: It Stays That Way
steps.text: The gallery remembers the size you picked, so it opens the same way next time.

lessons.title: Bismuth Full
lessons.summary: What the free edition holds, and what Bismuth Full adds.

steps.title: Free to Draw
steps.text: The free edition draws without limits: Symmetry, the Pattern Gallery, the everyday brushes, Fill, Trim, the Eraser and up to three layers.

steps.title: Bismuth Full
steps.text: Some tools are part of Bismuth Full: Repeat, Wallpaper and Fade, Constructions, Lattice, the Full brushes, Gradient Fill, Shape Builder, Print Stencil and more layers. Pick one and a short offer explains what Full adds.

steps.title: Unlock Once
steps.text: One purchase unlocks Bismuth Full for good, with no subscription. On a new iPad, open Preferences, then Bismuth Full, and tap Restore Purchase.

steps.title: Your Drawings Stay Yours
steps.text: Anything you make can always be opened, edited and exported as an image, whether or not you unlock Full.

lessons.title: The Lattice Panel
lessons.summary: Pictures first, then sections that fold, like the Pattern panel.

steps.title: Start From a Picture
steps.text: Open Lattice. The cards at the top are ready lattices and the ones you saved: tap one to use it. See All shows them all, in My Lattices and Ready.

steps.title: Open a Section
steps.text: Each section says what it is set to in one line. Tap a section's name to open it; opening another folds the first, so the panel stays short.

steps.title: Switches Open Their Section
steps.text: Recursion, Point Circles and Colour by Level have switches. Turn one on and its section opens; turn it off and it folds. Recursion holds a slider for each thing that changes level by level: thinner, fainter, smaller.

steps.title: Colour at the Top
steps.text: Tap the Lines or Points dot under Formations to choose a colour. The three dots with a spark pick colours for you; the dice picks a new shape and drawing.

steps.title: Save or Reset
steps.text: The bookmark at the top saves this lattice to My Lattices (long press its card to rename or remove it). Reset takes the shape back to one plain ring and keeps your colours.

lessons.title: Layer Groups
lessons.summary: Hide, move and fold several layers as one.

steps.title: Make a Group
steps.text: Open Layers, long press a layer and choose Group, then New Group with This Layer. Long press another layer and use Group to move it in. A lattice sent from Lattice always arrives as a group of its own.

steps.title: Hide It All
steps.text: Tap the eye on the group's row to hide or show every layer in it at once.

steps.title: Move It All
steps.text: Tap the arrows on the group's row, then drag, pinch or turn on the page: every layer in the group moves together. Tap the arrows again to place it.

steps.title: Fold and Rename
steps.text: Tap the row to fold the group to one line. Long press it to rename it or ungroup it. Every one of these undoes with a two-finger tap.

lessons.title: Tool Settings Bar
lessons.summary: Each tool's settings sit in one bar under the top bar.

steps.title: Pick a Tool
steps.text: Choose the Paint Bucket on the left rail.

steps.title: Its Settings, Up Top
steps.text: The bar under the top bar now holds what the Paint Bucket can do: Layer Fill, Dots or Page Background, Fill Outside, Gap Tolerance and Keep Lines. Every tool has its own bar, and a brush's bar has Size and Stabiliser.

steps.title: Lasso Too
steps.text: Choose the Lasso: its bar picks This Layer or All Layers. Draw around something, and the bar turns into the selection bar with Move, Duplicate, Mirror and more.

lessons.title: Your Puck, Your Buttons
lessons.summary: Choose which buttons sit around the touch puck.

steps.title: Open Touch Puck
steps.text: Open Preferences and choose Touch Puck. The preview shows your puck as it is on the page.

steps.title: Choose the Buttons
steps.text: Under Buttons, tap a chip to take that button off the puck or put it back: Undo, Redo, Eraser, Trim, Lift to Layer, Tool Switch, Mirror Curve and Mini Loupe. The eye that folds them all always stays.

steps.title: Size It
steps.text: Under Size, Puck Size, Halo Distance and Button Size work together, so the buttons never crowd the puck. Reset Puck Size puts them back.

lessons.title: Take a Photo or Scan the Body
lessons.summary: See the design on a photo you take, or on a 3D scan of the arm or leg.

steps.title: Take Photo
steps.text: In On a Photo, tap Take Photo beside Choose Photo. The camera opens; the photo you take is used just like one you chose, and it never leaves this iPad.

steps.title: Scan the Body
steps.text: On an iPad with LiDAR, tap Scan the Body. Move slowly around the arm, leg or back until the mesh covers it, then tap it. The bright circle is what is kept: set Keep to cover the part.

steps.title: Place It in 3D
steps.text: Tap Use Scan. The 3D Body Preview opens on your scan: tap it to place the design, then size, turn and paint as on the stock body. With Clients on, you choose who the scan is for, and your scans are kept under Clients.

lessons.title: Clients and Their Scans
lessons.summary: Keep each client's projects and body scans together, locked and only on this iPad.

steps.title: Open Clients
steps.text: In the 3D Body Preview, tap Clients in the top bar. Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode opens it, and it locks again whenever you leave Bismuth.

steps.title: Add a Client
steps.text: Tap New Client, type their name and a first project, then Add. Open a project to see its scans.

steps.title: Scan Into a Project
steps.text: In a project, tap Scan Into This Project. The scan is filed there and opens in 3D. Scanning from On a Photo asks who it is for, with the last project first.

steps.title: Tidy Up
steps.text: Tap a scan to open it in 3D. The … button renames it, moves it to another project or deletes it. Deleting always asks first.

knownIssues.title: Masks Can Look Confusing in Print Stencil
knownIssues.detail: Masks can show unexpected marks in the Print Stencil preview. A full review of masks is planned.
knownIssues.workaround: Clipping works as expected and can often be used instead.

knownIssues.title: Live Trace Can Miss Parts of a Picture
knownIssues.detail: Live Trace, an experimental tool, can leave some areas of a photo untraced.
knownIssues.workaround: Adjust the trace settings, or trace the missing parts by hand.

knownIssues.title: Restore Purchase in Test Builds
knownIssues.detail: Purchases cannot be restored in TestFlight builds. Everything is already open for testers.

knownIssues.title: New Drawing Can Close the App in Inches
knownIssues.detail: In the New Drawing sheet, tapping the Width or Height box after switching Units to in can close the app.
knownIssues.workaround: Pick a preset such as Letter or Tabloid, or set the size in mm or px.
